steps.title: Join from the catalogue
steps.change: Choose the join by asking which unmatched rows must stay. Use `LEFT JOIN` with the required population on the left when its unmatched rows must stay. Use `INNER JOIN` when only matches belong in the result, and `FULL OUTER JOIN` when unmatched rows on both sides belong. Here, all three catalogue products must stay, so start from `Products` and left join `OrderDetails`. Count distinct product IDs because one product can match several order lines.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT P.ProductID, P.Product, O.OrderDetailID, O.ProductID AS matched_product_id
FROM Products AS P
LEFT JOIN OrderDetails AS O ON P.ProductID = O.ProductID
ORDER BY P.ProductID, O.OrderDetailID;
steps.sql:
SELECT P.ProductID, P.Product, O.OrderDetailID, O.ProductID AS matched_product_id
FROM Products AS P
LEFT JOIN OrderDetails AS O ON P.ProductID = O.ProductID
ORDER BY P.ProductID, O.OrderDetailID;

steps.title: Count rows, sale lines, and distinct products
steps.change: Joined rows and distinct products answer different questions.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_after_join,
       COUNT(O.ProductID) AS sale_lines,
       COUNT(DISTINCT P.ProductID) AS listed_products,
       COUNT(DISTINCT (O.ProductID)) AS products_sold
steps.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_after_join,
       COUNT(O.ProductID) AS sale_lines,
       COUNT(DISTINCT P.ProductID) AS listed_products,
       COUNT(DISTINCT (O.ProductID)) AS products_sold
FROM Products AS P
LEFT JOIN OrderDetails AS O ON P.ProductID = O.ProductID;

steps.title: Calculate the percentage
steps.change: The fraction measures sold products out of all listed products.
steps.added_sql:
COUNT(DISTINCT (O.ProductID)) AS products_sold,
       ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT O.ProductID) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT P.ProductID), 2) AS pct_sold
